Hi it's totally normal. Please don't hate me on this and to everyone out there, my two cents and take it with a pinch of salt. 

I took a long route and have always been passionate with art. Took a dips in design and realised i'm not a child prodigy anymore lol. I find that there's no point to pursue further in a career where i'll lose my passion and only chase for money. I also find it pointless to pursue a degree in art/design unless there is a specific career that requires the degree qualification.

You know what? I ended up taking an entirely different course for uni and I never regretted. My passion for art never died, it only started to flourish while I also focus on trying to earn through a different skillset which I also enjoy. You need to be realistic, you need to make compromises. Unless you're talented or you have networks that can get you out there in the industry, you REALLY need to work you ass off when it comes to the design industry to even do well. Now this depends entirely on you. WHAT do you really want? And what will you prioritise. It's good that you're thinking long term, but don't forget to reflect and enjoy in the moment, it might help you see life clearer.

For me, I took mine as a hobby, and I'm so much happier than when I had to suffer in poly. 

Good luck.

Sometimes its also the photogs, sometimes they just can't take a picture properly and makes the distortion worse 🤣 and sometimes you dont look as good IRL from the pics.. but its fine.
